statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-54696 (GHSA-x2f5-4prf-w687): in the Ruby json gem from 2.9.0 and before 2.19.9, JSON.dump(obj, io) and JSON::State#generate(obj, io) can write past the generator's internal buffer when a streamed string lands near the 16 KB IO buffer size, because fbuffer_do_inc_capa compared the request with the buffer's total capacity instead of the space left (a heap out-of-bounds write, demonstrated as a crash): https://github.com/ruby/json/security/advisories/GHSA-x2f5-4prf-w687. It is fixed in json 2.19.9 by https://github.com/ruby/json/commit/996bac686d64e4e3aaeae03b14a7f9ee9695ebdb, released in v2.19.9 as https://github.com/ruby/json/commit/fd6a65bd08e5f3a429c03919ebfd8dd19158f095, which reworks fbuffer_do_inc_capa in ext/json/ext/fbuffer/fbuffer.h so the IO path flushes and then sizes the buffer from the bytes already held; it drops the IO path's comparison of the buffer capacity with 16383 (FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE): https://github.com/ruby/json/releases/tag/v2.19.9. Every Ruby 4.0 release bundles json 2.18 (2.18.0, and 2.18.3 in 4.0.10), so the fixed json in the builds below is a DHI update of the json default gem. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-4.0 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as published on 2026-11-28, 654 package files across both architectures, checked each against its repository index checksum and listed every file in them. The json default gem, with its compiled generator.so, ships in ruby-4.0-libs. Other packages from this source carry json-named files that are not the json library, such as debug symbols for the json extensions (ruby-4.0-dbg), ri documentation (ruby-4.0-doc), rbs's json.rbs type signature and JSON Schema files (ruby4.0-rbs), rdoc's JSON index generator (ruby4.0-rdoc) and typeprof's typeprof.conf.jsonc (ruby4.0-typeprof). The json gem's usr/lib/ruby/4.0.0/json/version.rb, identical to the upstream release file, reads 2.18.0 in 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1 and 4.0.2-r1, 2.19.2 in 4.0.2-r2 through 4.0.6-r3, and 2.19.9 in 4.0.6-r4 and every later build. We also disassembled fbuffer_do_inc_capa in generator.so of every published ruby-4.0-libs build on both architectures, locating it with the symbol table in the matching ruby-4.0-dbg package: up to and including 4.0.6-r3 it still compares the buffer capacity with 16383 and grows the buffer to 16383 on the IO path, the code the fix removes, and from 4.0.6-r4 that comparison is gone. Both architectures agree for every build. The range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.6-r4, the first build with json 2.19.9.

Every Ruby 4.0 release bundles json 2.18 (2.18.0, and 2.18.3 in 4.0.10), so the fixed json in the builds below is a DHI update of the json default gem. The DHI Debian 13 repository publishes the ruby-4.0 source as the ruby-4.0 and ruby-4.0-dev packages, 81 versions on amd64 and arm64: 4.0.5-0 to 4.0.5-6, 4.0.6-0 to 4.0.6-50, 4.0.7-0 to 4.0.7-19, 4.0.9-0, 4.0.9-1 and 4.0.10-0. The json default gem, with its compiled generator.so, ships in ruby-4.0; ruby-4.0-dev contains no json file. We read the md5sums manifest in the control archive of every published ruby-4.0 and ruby-4.0-dev package on both architectures as published on 2026-11-28: usr/lib/ruby/4.0.0/json/version.rb matches the json 2.19.2 release file in ruby-4.0 4.0.5-0 through 4.0.7-1 and the json 2.19.9 release file in 4.0.7-2 through 4.0.10-0. We downloaded ruby-4.0 4.0.5-0, 4.0.6-50, 4.0.7-1, 4.0.7-2 and 4.0.10-0 on both architectures, checked against the repository index SHA256, and disassembled their generator.so: 4.0.5-0, 4.0.6-50 and 4.0.7-1 still compare the buffer capacity with 16383 on the IO path, the code the fix removes, and 4.0.7-2 and 4.0.10-0 do not. Both architectures agree for every build. The range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.7-2, the first build with json 2.19.9.
